data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies sky-view factor (SVF) as the SINGLE mechanism explaining cross-city variation in the nocturnal UHI gap, but SVF actually governs only one component of nocturnal cooling — longwave radiative loss to the sky. On a clear, calm night, the dominant reason the countryside cools faster is that it has MORE stored heat to release per unit area (from daytime sensible heat sequestration), and the city has LESS because much daytime energy went into latent heat via evapotranspiration rather than thermal storage. Across cities, the single largest source of variation in the nocturnal gap is differences in impervious surface fraction / vegetation (which controls how much daytime energy becomes stored sensible heat vs. latent heat), not SVF. A desert city with low SVF but no moisture and minimal thermal mass would show a SMALLER nocturnal gap than a humid city with high SVF and abundant thermal mass, directly contradicting the target's claim that lower SVF produces a larger gap and that SVF is the single best cross-city modulator. The target's own mechanism text tacitly acknowledges this by listing 'impervious low-albedo, high-heat-capacity surfaces' as the storage driver, yet names SVF — a cooling-rate modifier — as the single cross-city controller, conflating the mechanism that creates the gap (differential stored-heat release) with a secondary radiative-geometry factor.
